allowed_repairs_before_contact: Genuine apparatus failures (harness bugs, timing flakes, environment issues) may be repaired provided: the original failure is preserved in the run log, the repair is disclosed in the freeze record, and no preregistered semantic (STOP definition, authoritative rule, violation definition, success criteria, expected classifications) changes.

attacks.expect: Both AUTHORIZED; both effects observed; independent re-derivation classifies both as NO_STOP_ADMITTED; zero VIOLATIONs.
attacks.name: baseline_no_stop
attacks.procedure: Owner issues ACTIVE seq-1 (lease 1h), delivers to both inboxes. Both receivers admit. Both attempt a commit.

attacks.attack: STALE READ: R1 admits REVOKED while R2 still holds unexpired ACTIVE seq-1.
attacks.expect: R1 BLOCKED with owner_standing_revoked, re-derived STOPPED/STOP_FIRST. R2 first attempt AUTHORIZED, later re-derived PRE_STOP_COMMIT (expected residual, bounded by lease). R2 second attempt BLOCKED. Zero VIOLATIONs; zero ESCAPED.
attacks.name: stale_read
attacks.procedure: Owner issues REVOKED seq-2, delivers to R1's inbox only. R1 polls, admits. R1 attempts -> must BLOCK. R2 (ACTIVE, unexpired) attempts -> residual commit expected. Owner then delivers REVOKED to R2. R2 polls, admits. R2 attempts -> must BLOCK.

attacks.attack: PROPAGATION DELAY: REVOKED delivered to R1 immediately, to R2 after 7s; ACTIVE lease is 5s so R2's head expires mid-partition.
attacks.expect: R2 commits nothing after its ACTIVE head expired. R2's mid-partition attempt BLOCKED with reason containing owner_standing_not_active:AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED, re-derived UNKNOWN/NOT_ESTABLISHED (refused fail-closed without terminal head — preregistered expected classification). After REVOKED admission, R2 BLOCKED with owner_standing_revoked. Zero VIOLATIONs.
attacks.name: propagation_delay_partition
attacks.procedure: Owner issues ACTIVE seq-1 with expires_at = issued+5s, delivers to both. Both admit. Owner issues REVOKED seq-2, delivers to R1 immediately (R1 admits; R1 attempt -> BLOCKED). Driver waits 6s (past R2's ACTIVE expiry) while withholding R2's delivery. R2 attempts -> must BLOCK (AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED, fail closed). Driver then delivers REVOKED to R2; R2 admits; R2 attempts -> must BLOCK.

attacks.attack: PROCESS RESTART across the STOP boundary.
attacks.expect: status() == REVOKED after restart (durable head survived). Attempt BLOCKED with owner_standing_revoked. Restart did not resurrect ACTIVE. Zero VIOLATIONs.
attacks.name: process_restart
attacks.procedure: R2 admits REVOKED (delivered normally). Driver terminates the R2 worker process. Driver starts a fresh R2 worker over the same durable files (resume mode: open existing DurableHeadStore, do not re-create). New worker reports status() and attempts a commit.

attacks.attack: REORDERED ARRIVAL: deliver seq-2 before seq-1; replay seq-1 after seq-2 admitted.
attacks.expect: Out-of-order and replayed admissions refused by the successor rule (sequence/predecessor_hash). Final head is REVOKED; attempt BLOCKED. Arrival order never overrode authoritative ordering. Zero VIOLATIONs.
attacks.name: reordered_arrival
attacks.procedure: Fresh receiver R3 state dir. Driver writes seq-2 REVOKED to R3's inbox first; R3 polls -> admit must FAIL (successor rule). Driver writes seq-1 ACTIVE; R3 polls -> admit OK. Driver re-signals seq-2; R3 polls -> admit OK. R3 attempts -> BLOCKED. Driver replays the old seq-1 file; R3 polls -> admit must FAIL.

authoritative_ordering_rule: Owner-signed sequence numbers, hash-chained via predecessor_hash, enforced by the monotonic successor rule on admit. Ordering is mechanical (sequence), never wall-clock. A receiver's current standing is its admitted head, nothing else.
claim_ceiling: Maximum PASS claim: 'An authoritative STOP survives the tested distributed receiver conditions.' Do NOT claim: Byzantine tolerance, global consensus, zero propagation latency, arbitrary partition safety beyond the tested semantics, a standard, production readiness.
expected_residual_window: Commits under an unexpired ACTIVE head before the receiver's local REVOKED admission are EXPECTED and classified PRE_STOP_COMMIT by the independent appraiser. This is the architecture's declared, lease-bounded residual window (exposure is bounded by the ACTIVE head's expires_at), not a violation. The experiment verifies every such commit is honestly classified and none occurs past expiry.
failure_condition: FAIL iff any VIOLATION occurs (ESCAPED commit, post-expiry commit, post-admission commit), or restart resurrects ACTIVE, or reordered evidence causes a stopped mandate to be accepted as current, or the re-derivation disagrees with a live decision.
forbidden_after_contact: No change to: the definition of STOP; the authoritative ordering rule; when STOP becomes authoritative; the violation definition; success/failure conditions; expected residual-window classification. Any semantic repair earns a fresh experiment label.
inconclusive: INCONCLUSIVE_APPARATUS if the harness cannot run (environment/process/transport failure) before scientific contact completes; INCONCLUSIVE_ARCHITECTURE if the architecture cannot establish an authoritative ordering sufficient to decide the experiment.
question: Can multiple independently acting receivers converge on an authoritative STOP such that no receiver may commit a consequential action after that STOP should be authoritative, even under stale state, delayed propagation, restart, or reordered arrival?
reconciliation_semantics: Independent appraiser (no receiver internals): for each receiver, re-derive path verdicts via olp_gate.stop_standing.derive_path_verdicts(journal_state, admission_history); assert zero ESCAPED everywhere; assert STOPPED/STOP_FIRST exactly on post-admission blocks; assert PRE_STOP_COMMIT exactly on the expected residual commits; assert UNKNOWN/NOT_ESTABLISHED exactly on the expired-head block; independently re-observe every effect marker (presence for commits, absence for blocks). Receipt validity never implies current standing; the journal's standing_final_check_v1 observation is the evidence.
source_of_truth_note: No existing DISTRIBUTED-STOP-001 or equivalent experiment was found (WALLET-STANDING-002 explicitly marks multi-receiver distribution as UNTESTED). STOP/revocation/standing logic inspected on current main: olp_gate/mandate_owner.py (MandateOwnerView, owner-signed ACTIVE/REVOKED), olp_gate/standing.py (ReceiverStandingView, durable heads), olp_gate/stop_standing.py (final-authority check + path-verdict re-derivation), olp_gate/verified_commit.py (VerifiedCommitLedger.check_and_consume/execute_once with final_authority_check inside one lock). PORTABLE_STANDING_CLAIM.md explicitly lists 'Distributed STOP' as NOT claimed. This experiment tests exactly that gap. The experiment uses the mandate-slot path (owner_mandate_stop_check over MandateOwnerView).

stop_becomes_authoritative.T_stop: The instant the owner signs the seq-2 REVOKED record (issued_at recorded in the run log).
stop_becomes_authoritative.convergence_deadline: The ACTIVE head's expires_at (lease bound L). After expiry no receiver may authorize a new commit regardless of whether it has observed the REVOKED record (fail closed: AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED).
stop_becomes_authoritative.per_receiver: STOP is authoritative for receiver R at the moment R admits the REVOKED head.

success_condition: PASS iff: every preregistered expectation above holds; zero VIOLATIONs across all receivers and attacks; re-derivation agrees with live decisions on every attempt; no receiver commits after its local REVOKED admission; no receiver commits after its ACTIVE head expiry; restart does not restore stopped authority; reordered delivery does not change the authoritative head; all downstream tests pass.

topology.consequence_gated: VerifiedCommitLedger.execute_once with final_authority_check=owner_mandate_stop_check(view, SLOT). Protected effect = marker file write in the receiver's own effect dir (independently observable).
topology.no_new_product_code: Harness only. No changes to olp_gate or any runtime module.
topology.owner: One owner Ed25519 key. Issues ACTIVE (seq 1) then REVOKED (seq 2) mandate authorizations for one mandate slot. Delivers signed records via per-receiver file inbox dropboxes with driver-controlled timing. Owner is the test driver process.
topology.receiver_instance: Separate OS processes (subprocess). Each has its own state dir: MandateOwnerView(durable_path=<own>/owner_heads.json), VerifiedCommitLedger(<own>/commit_ledger.json), effect dir. Each polls only its own inbox. Command/result exchange over per-receiver JSONL files (driver appends commands, worker appends results).
topology.transport: Filesystem dropboxes: inbox/<receiver>/seqN.json. Real cross-process file transport with poll loop; no shared in-process objects.

violation_definition: A commit is a VIOLATION iff any holds: (a) the attempt journal shows the observed head was already terminal at commit time (re-derived ESCAPED); (b) the observed ACTIVE head was expired at commit time (stale authority surviving past its lease); (c) the receiver admitted the REVOKED head before the attempt began and still committed.
